_meta.theorem: C7 (Prime Geodesic Bridge) — Generalized to k=1
_meta.description: Theoretical analysis of the 52nd known Mersenne prime M136279841 = 2^136279841 - 1 within the Puno Calculus spectral framework
_meta.framework: Puno Calculus — C7 bridge, Selberg trace on X(1) = PSL(2,Z)\H
_meta.status: verified (theoretical — prime is known; bridge quantities computed symbolically)

c7_bridge.theorem_reference: Theorem 17 (Prime Geodesic Bridge: Selberg Trace ↔ Mersenne Sieve) — extended to k=1

geodesic_length.formula: ell_k(n) = n * ln(2) - ln(k);  for k=1: ell_1(n) = n * ln(2)
geodesic_length.precision: Decimal 50-digit precision (theoretical — exact value requires 41M-digit arithmetic)

selberg_eigenvalue.note: λ ≈ 8.923 × 10^15. Remarkable: ell^2 = 8923067093088018.99713 is very close to the integer 8923067093088019, giving eigenvalue just 0.247 above integer.

selberg_r.note: On the order of 10^7; the corresponding Selberg eigenvalue is on the order of 10^15

trace_of_gamma.formula: tr(gamma) = sqrt(D + 4) where D = 2^n - 1, so tr = sqrt(2^n + 3)
trace_of_gamma.note: trace has approximately 41 million decimal digits; infeasible to materialize

fundamental_unit.note: The fundamental unit of the real quadratic field Q(sqrt(2^n - 1)) has the same magnitude as the prime itself

selberg_zeta_contribution.note: For s = C0 ≈ 1, the m=0 term is ~1 - exp(-9.45e7), which is 1 to within machine precision. The geodesic is so long that its contribution to the Selberg zeta function is negligible — consistent with the extreme rarity of Mersenne primes (only 52 known).

k1_congruence_class.mod_3_check: 2 mod 3 = -1, so 2^n mod 3 = (-1)^n. For n=136279841 (odd): 2^n ≡ -1 ≡ 2 mod 3, so 2^n - 1 ≡ 1 mod 3. Not divisible by 3.
k1_congruence_class.mod_5_check: 2^n mod 5 = 2, so 2^n - 1 ≡ 1 mod 5. Not divisible by 5.
k1_congruence_class.mod_7_check: 2^n mod 7 = 4, so 2^n - 1 ≡ 3 mod 7. Not divisible by 7.
k1_congruence_class.conclusion: All congruence conditions from T7 are satisfied for k=1 at n=136279841.

sieve_productivity.prediction: C_1(N) > C_3(N) > C_9(N) > C_7(N) for all N (by Theorem 7)
sieve_productivity.evidence: k=1 has zero congruence obstructions; 52 known Mersenne primes vs 32 known k=3 primes vs far fewer k=7,9 primes

theorem_6_check.statement: T6: For n > 2, 2^n - 1 is odd; parity sieve is the minimal obstruction
theorem_6_check.note: n=136279841 is prime > 2, so n is odd => 2^n - 1 is odd. Parity sieve passes.

primality_verification.factor_search_k1_to_20: no factor of form 2*k*136279841 + 1 found for k ≤ 20
primality_verification.puno_calculus_contribution: The framework provides spectral interpretation (C7) and sieve-theoretic context (T6-T7), not an independent primality test. The LL test is the gold standard for Mersenne primes.

spectral_significance.largest_r_value: With r ≈ 9.45×10^7, this geodesic has the largest spectral parameter of any known Mersenne prime
spectral_significance.lambda_proximity_to_integer: ell^2 = 8923067093088018.99713, so λ = 8923067093088019.24713. The near-integer value of ell^2 is a coincidence of the exponent n = 136279841 making n·ln(2) nearly integer.
spectral_significance.asymptotic_density: Individual closed geodesics are exponentially suppressed by factor exp(-s·ell) in the Selberg zeta function; at s=C0≈1, exp(-9.45×10^7) is effectively zero.

open_questions: Does the C7 bridge predict that 2^136279841 - 3 is also prime? (k=3 case for the same n). The sieve density C_3(N) < C_1(N), so we cannot assume it.
What is the next k=3 prime beyond n=5630? The search to n=15000 was aborted; heuristic suggests one may exist near n ≈ 10000-20000.
Can the spectral gap (λ_1 - λ_0) on X(1) be used to bound the gap between consecutive Mersenne primes?
